newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK red chips down in choppy trade, firm tone seen.
newsitem.headline: HK red chips down in choppy trade, firm tone seen.

text.p: The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index eased in choppy morning trade on Tuesday, but the red-chip index was still expected to trend firmer ahead of the territory's handover to China next week, brokers said.
The red-chip index slipped 4.66 points or 0.15 percent to 3,061.97 at midday after bouncing off a morning low of 2,997.34.
The blue-chip Hang Seng Index fell 61.92 or 0.41 percent to 14,959.31 at midsession.
"The sector is expected to remain firm or even outperform the market in the next couple of day ahead of the handover," said Tony Yung, research manager at Tai Fook Securities.
"Investors are still focused on those asset injection concept stocks and that will support the index," Yung said.
Red chips, Hong Kong-based companies with Chinese financial backing, have been buoyed by hopes of favourable asset injections by their mainland parents.

Even though red-chip sentiment is expected to remain solid, a sharp rally in the sector was unlikely in the near run because short-term investors may unload weighting ahead of the five-day handover weekend, brokers said.

"Some people may want to take profit before the holiday, obviously there will be a little bit of sellling pressure," said Kent Rossiter of institutional sales at Nikko Securities. "I wouldn't expect too much on the upside (in the next few days)."
Brokers said people were also expected to stay on the sidelines following the announcement of guidelines by mainland regulators on asset injections and listings by red chips.
Analysts generally said they welcomed the move although it might have a psychological impact in the medium term.
Among red-chip stocks, Guangdong Investment Ltd fell HK$0.10 to HK$10.70, and Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd dropped HK$0.10 to HK$42.90.
But, COSCO Pacific rose HK$0.50 to HK$14.85 and China Resources up HK$0.20 to HK$30.00.
Analysts generally said they expected red chip stocks to undergo a correction after the handover.

"We expect a major correction to emerge after the handover because hot money and investment funds may switch out from the market," Yung said. "Fund managers may reallocate their funds in the beginning of their fiscal year second half."
